description: Buffer overflow reachable ONLY through an interrupt handler (vector-table slot 16, IRQ0/UART0_IRQHandler) -- the prompt's 2nd named hard problem: reachability must consider 'any entry point (interrupt handlers included)'. main() never touches the vulnerable state.

cases.reason: irq_buf[8] is written at irq_buf_idx with no bound check. Each UART0 IRQ delivers one more byte; if more than 8 bytes arrive without a '\n' resetting the index, the write overflows irq_buf. Reachability analysis must treat vector[16] (IRQ0) as a CFG root independent of main()'s call graph -- it is NOT reachable by walking calls from main/Reset_Handler alone.
cases.verification_strategy: Full NVIC/interrupt-controller emulation is out of scope for the MVP. Per the pipeline's step 4 ('seed emulation directly at the finding's entry point'), dynamic verification should seed the emulator at UART0_IRQHandler's address directly (treating it like a callable entry with its own stack frame) and drive it with >8 injected bytes across repeated invocations, rather than attempting to simulate real interrupt delivery/preemption from main()'s wfi loop.
failure_modes_if_wrong: Reachability rooted only at main()/Reset_Handler: UART0_IRQHandler has no incoming call edge from main -> wrongly classified unreachable/FP.
Emulation that only ever runs from reset and never seeds/injects at the ISR: main() sits in 'wfi' forever, ISR body never executes -> wrongly reported Inconclusive.
